thesis: XP's issuer-filed 2Q26 materials identify IFRS as the reporting framework and separately label adjusted/non-GAAP metrics. The confirmed quarter showed client assets of R$1.535 trillion (+12% year over year), net inflow of R$28 billion (+188%), net revenue growth of 9%, and EBT growth of 15%, supporting a long read alongside the 22.11% 60-calendar-day move and 3.37x volume signal. The strongest counter-evidence is only 1% active-client growth, a 13% sequential decline in retail daily average trades, and lower adjusted ROAE year over year; it does not overturn the read because inflows, revenue, gross profit, and EBT all advanced in the same disclosed quarter. Today's overbought-RSI commentary is technical rather than a new company disclosure and does not strengthen the fundamental case.
invalidation: Client net inflows turn negative or the next issuer report shows contracting net revenue and EBT without a resolved one-time explanation.

thesis: Sasol's confirmed audited FY2026 IFRS results reported issuer-reported basic EPS of R18.99, adjusted EBITDA up 17%, operating cash generation up 22%, and net debt down 11% to US$3.3 billion, supporting a long read alongside the 22.13% 60-calendar-day move, 2.50x volume, and proximity to the 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is the absence of a final dividend, elevated working capital, major impairments, and unresolved material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting; it does not overturn the read because KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on the IFRS financial statements and the disclosed cash generation and debt reduction are concrete. Ongoing legal matters disclosed in the 20-F did not identify a scheduled hearing, ruling, trial, or compliance deadline in the next approximately 90 days, so no active_litigation tag is applied.
invalidation: Net debt reverses higher, operating cash generation deteriorates materially, or the next filing reports a material misstatement or failure to progress the disclosed ICFR remediation.

thesis: Neogen's September 8 company announcement confirms an October 7 Investor Day focused on its strategic transformation, while its U.S. GAAP FY2026 filing and fourth-quarter release showed 4.3% core revenue growth, 5.8% core Food Safety growth, positive operating cash flow, and resolution of most Animal Safety supply challenges. These facts support a long read alongside the 23.16% 60-calendar-day move and 2.60x volume signal. The strongest counter-evidence is the fourth-quarter net loss and an 8.2% year-over-year decline in Animal Safety revenue; it does not overturn the read because core growth accelerated and supply availability improved, but the pending Investor Day caps conviction at medium.
invalidation: The October 7 Investor Day fails to provide measurable operational milestones, or subsequent results show renewed supply disruption and reversal of core Food Safety growth.

thesis: The held BOXX position continues to match the fund's disclosed objective as an options-based alternative to an ultrashort-duration bond position. As of September 8 the sponsor reported a 3.36% average yield to option expiration, 12 average days to expiration, NAV of $118.17 versus a $118.13 market price, and a 0.01% 30-day median bid/ask spread; the latest SEC portfolio report also confirms the fund remains active. The strongest counter-evidence is that box-spread, tax, counterparty, liquidity, and distribution behavior is not identical to holding Treasury bills; it does not overturn the hold thesis because the current sponsor data show short maturity, tight spread, and close NAV tracking. Searches found no qualifying scheduled litigation event or completed governance-history event tied to the fund in the required windows.
invalidation: The fund develops a persistent material discount to NAV, materially wider trading spreads, a significant strategy or tax-treatment change, or a regulatory filing indicating disruption to the box-spread program.
